findings.text: blocking: adding "refused": True to the in-flight refusals (code at :3126, figure at :3429) makes an ordinary in-flight review read as a refused landing attempt. reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:1230 computes `refused = ... or bool(report.get("refused"))`, so a delivered run whose review is simply still running is now recorded with queue_landing._record_attempt(status="refused") at :1244 and reported status "review-refused" at :1268, where before it reached _record_awaiting_review and status "awaiting-review". That refusal record is what reckon/crew/obligations.py:3495 turns into a `landing-refused` duty reading "automatic landing refused: repair code review: a review of run ... is already in flight ...", so a coordinator is told to repair a healthy review that is merely running. The winner-naming change needs no `refused` key; either drop the key from the two in-flight refusals or teach pending_landing._repair_review_wait to read an in-flight review as awaiting rather than refused.

non-blocking: the figure-review in-flight refusal's new winner-naming text (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3429) has no deterministic assertion. The eight-at-once case asserts the winner appears in each loser's reason, and test_a_code_review_and_a_figure_review_each_get_one (:387) only counts the launched runs; the figure losers usually lose at the claim, whose reason already named the winner, so reverting the figure in-flight sentence would leave the suite green. Add a case that stands a young figure review in flight and asserts its reason names it.
